Leak Detection & Moisture Survey

Find the source — not just the stain.

Repainting over a damp patch never fixes the leak. Using moisture meters and thermal imaging, we trace water back to its source non-destructively — no hacking required — so it can be repaired once, correctly.

What's included

  • Non-destructive moisture mapping
  • Thermal imaging tracing
  • Source identification (roof / pipe / seepage)
  • Wet area waterproofing check
  • Repair method recommendation

What you receive

  • Leak source report with evidence
  • Moisture readings map
  • Targeted repair recommendation

Why It Matters

Repainting a Damp Patch Fixes Nothing

Find the Source, Not the Stain

Water travels — the wet patch is rarely where the leak actually is

Non-Destructive Investigation

No hacking, no demolition — instruments locate it through finished surfaces

Repair Once, Correctly

Guessing means paying for repeated repairs that never solve the problem

Evidence for Neighbour Disputes

Leaks from the unit above are a common dispute — readings settle it objectively

Targeted Repair Recommendation

Your contractor gets a precise location and method, not a vague complaint

Stop Damage Spreading

Prolonged damp destroys finishes, plaster and eventually the structure itself

How It Works

4 Stages of a Leak Investigation

Non-destructive from start to finish — we find the source before anyone breaks a wall

1

Symptom Mapping

We record where the damp appears, when it worsens, and its history

2

Moisture Survey

Systematic moisture readings across the area to find the wettest concentration

3

Thermal Tracing

Thermal imaging follows the moisture path back through walls, ceilings and slabs

4

Source Report & Method

Identified source, supporting readings and the correct repair method to fix it

Moisture Classification

Every Reading Classified

Moisture readings mapped across the area so the wettest point leads us to the source

Dry

Normal reading for the material — no moisture concern

Elevated

Above normal — monitor, may be residual or seasonal

Wet

Active moisture present — a source exists and must be traced

Saturated

Material fully wet — ongoing leak with damage already occurring

Investigation Scope

6 Sources We Trace

The same stain can come from six different places — we identify which one

Bathroom Above

Most common in stratified homes

Typical Signs
Ceiling stain below wet areaWorsens after showeringPeeling ceiling paintMusty smell
How We Trace It
Moisture mappingThermal imagingWater ponding test

Roof & Valley Gutters

Worse after heavy rain

Typical Signs
Leak only during rainStains near roof junctionsBlocked valley guttersFailed flashing
How We Trace It
Visual & drone surveyMoisture mappingRain simulation

External Wall Seepage

Driven rain & wall cracks

Typical Signs
Damp on internal face of external wallFollows crack linesEfflorescence (white salt)Worse on the weather side
How We Trace It
Moisture mappingThermal imagingCrack survey

Concealed Pipe Leak

Inside walls & floors

Typical Signs
Damp present in dry weatherConstant, not rain-relatedUnexplained water bill riseWarm patch (hot water line)
How We Trace It
Thermal imagingMoisture mappingPressure test

Waterproofing Failure

Wet areas & balconies

Typical Signs
Damp at wet area perimeterBalcony leaking to unit belowFailed membrane at upturnsWater tracking under tiles
How We Trace It
Water ponding testMoisture mappingThermal imaging

Condensation (Not a Leak)

Often misdiagnosed

Typical Signs
Damp on cold surfacesWorse in air-conditioned roomsMould on wardrobes & cornersNo source found upstream
How We Trace It
Moisture mappingThermal imagingVentilation assessment
